name: Shot glass lip challenge
lead: The shot glass lip challenge is a social-media trend in which people press the rim of a small glass or similar container over their mouth and create suction, so that the lips swell temporarily and look fuller. It is a do-it-yourself variant of suction lip plumping, which medical references describe as drawing blood into the lips by vacuum pressure and producing short-lived swelling.[1][1]

The trend was dubbed the "Kylie Jenner Challenge" in 2015, after speculation about Jenner's lips and her admission on television that she had had lip augmentation; Wikipedia notes there was no indication she used suction herself.[2] Participants share before-and-after images or videos of the fuller-looking lips.

Clinical references on lip augmentation note that bruising and swelling are common after lip procedures and can last from several days to a week, and list irritation, bleeding and uneven lips among possible effects.[1] No published clinical studies have examined the shot glass challenge itself.

chain: Glass held over the mouth with suction
Lips look temporarily fuller and more defined
angle.text: Suction draws blood into the lips and makes them swell for a short time. Participants post before-and-after photos to show the temporary fuller look without fillers.

infobox: Suction applied with a glass or cup

paras: Participants hold a glass or comparable container against the mouth and draw air out so that suction pulls the lips into it, then share before-and-after images or videos. The effect they seek is temporary fullness, similar to what commercial suction lip pumps are marketed to produce.[1][1]

Wikipedia's lip augmentation article separates two non-surgical product types: lip plumpers, which irritate the skin of the lips with ingredients such as capsaicin to cause temporary swelling, and suction pumps, which use vacuum pumping to increase blood pressure in the lips.[1]

The trend took off in 2015 around Kylie Jenner, whose enhanced lips drew publicity. After her May 2015 episode of Keeping Up with the Kardashians in which she acknowledged lip augmentation, people began suctioning their lips into a small glass and the practice was called the Kylie Jenner Challenge.[2] Jenner said she was not trying to encourage young people to look like her or think that is how they should look.[2]

Suction pumps work by drawing blood into the lips; medical sources describe the resulting swelling as temporary.[1][1] News and social-media coverage of the trend has focused on bruising and swelling after attempts; this article does not cite individual reports.
No studies found. Research on lip augmentation more broadly concerns fillers, fat transfer and implants rather than home suction.[1]

timeline.event: Kylie Jenner acknowledges lip augmentation on television in May, and the suction trend is named the Kylie Jenner Challenge.[2]

card.summary: A viral suction trick that swells the lips for a short time; no studies exist and bruising is the commonly reported result.
card.note: Reported bruising and swelling; no clinical studies.

quick.overview:
The shot glass lip challenge involves creating suction over the lips with a small glass so they swell and look fuller for a short while. It spread as a social-media trend.

No clinical research has tested it. Medical sources describe suction plumping as causing temporary swelling.
quick.mechanism: Suction draws blood into the lip tissue, producing short-lived swelling rather than any lasting change to lip structure.
quick.risks: Bruising and swelling are the commonly reported effects of lip suction and lip procedures generally. There is no regulatory or clinical guidance specific to the trend.
